conventions.convention: The plane has coordinates (x₁,x₂), its standard orientation, and Hodge star *dx₁=dx₂, *dx₂=−dx₁. The covariant derivative is D_A=d−iA and dA=B dx₁∧dx₂.
Parameters e and ξ are positive, κ=2e²ξ, and the energy density is B²/(2e²)+|D_Aq|²+e²(|q|²−ξ)²/2. Positive critical equations are (D₁+iD₂)q=0 and B=e²(ξ−|q|²).

A divisor has distinct centers with positive integer multiplicities, degree N equal to their sum, and empty divisor of degree zero. Its scalar equation has source 4π times the divisor and center subtraction h−2m_j log|z−z_j|.

A boundary sector requires q=ρ exp(i(nθ+φ)) outside a disk, with ρ>0 and real single-valued periodic φ, and uniform limits ρ→√ξ and φ→0. Global gauge transformations use smooth real-valued χ on the entire plane.
The exterior unwinding gauge is local; only the degree-zero phase correction relative to nθ is removed globally. Canonical end representatives retain exterior phase nθ.

Cylinder competitors have finite energy, finite-energy slices of fixed winding n and flux 2πn, uniform exterior vacuum behavior, the uniform angular one-form limit, and vanishing limiting side flux. End traces are fixed after global degree-zero gauge cleanup.

The analytic results use ZF plus full Axiom of Choice, including the Countable Choice assumptions of the imported analytic suppliers. All assigned items are mathematical model statements, without empirical premises.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming AC, for every e,ξ>0 and effective finite divisor D, the scalar Taubes equation with the prescribed logarithmic singularities and h→0 at infinity has a unique solution. Its displayed reconstruction gives smooth critical fields of finite energy and flux 2πN, with exponential scalar-derivative and gauge-invariant field decay at every rate below √κ. Negative winding follows by conjugation and A↦−A.

For κ>0 and a finite effective divisor of degree N, the displayed lower barrier with a≥4N/κ and the disk upper barrier bound a monotone Dirichlet iteration. It converges pointwise and in H¹ to a smooth desingularized disk solution u_R with u_-≤u_R≤0; after subtracting the fixed logarithmic singular function, the solutions have R-independent local W²,p and C²,α bounds.

Assuming AC, every smooth finite-energy field pair in the stated winding-n boundary sector satisfies E(A,q)≥2πξ|n|, with the displayed exact signed square-completion identity. Arbitrary-divisor reconstructed fields attain equality, are absolute transverse minima, and have zero first variation and nonnegative second variation under smooth compactly supported variations.

Defines smooth connection/Higgs pairs on the plane, their critical energy, winding boundary sector, global real gauge transformations, signed critical equations, finite effective divisors, scalar Taubes data and magnetic flux.

Assuming AC, for any two fixed admissible winding-n end traces in canonical exterior gauge and any selected arbitrary-divisor planar minimizer, there are ℓ>0 and finite C₀,C₁ independent of L such that T_n L≤inf ℰ_L≤T_n(L−2ℓ)+C₀+C₁ for L≥2ℓ, where T_n=2πξ|n|. Identical minimizing ends attain T_n L exactly.

published_dependencies.used_for: Full choice base, including Countable Choice for analytic suppliers and diagonal/radius selections.
Weak-derivative Sobolev classes and norms in the disk resolvent and convergence argument.
Existence, uniqueness and coercive norm estimate for the real shifted Dirichlet resolvent.
Resolvent positivity, barrier comparisons, local bounds and uniqueness comparisons with nonnegative zeroth-order coefficient.
Weak-to-W²,p regularity of bounded disk solutions for p>2 on smooth disks.
C²,α regularity up to the disk boundary after establishing Hölder right-hand sides.
W²,p-to-C¹,β bounds on disks for β<1−2/p.
Verification that the bounded smooth disks satisfy the extension-domain hypothesis of Sobolev embedding.
Uniform local estimates for already smooth desingularized solutions and exterior derivative-decay estimates.
Local Hölder estimates, smooth bootstrapping and exponential derivative estimates for the constant-coefficient Laplacian.
Hilbert-space structure of H¹ and its closed zero-boundary subspace for Lax–Milgram.
Boundedness of the resolvent form and functional, convergence estimates and circle-current estimates.
Absolute bounds on integral pairings in the resolvent argument.
L² convergence of the bounded monotone iteration and exhaustion limits of nonnegative plane integrals.
Logarithmic distribution identity, disk square-completion boundary terms, flux identities and side-cylinder flux.
Strict negativity of the nonempty-divisor scalar solution through the auxiliary three-dimensional subharmonic function.
Radial slicing of energy densities and the scalar flux calculation.
Identification of angular measure with dθ and circle arc length with r dθ.
Uniform subsequence convergence of finite derivative tuples on compact disks before diagonal extraction.
Absolutely integrable polar-product calculations, good-radius selection and slicing of finite cylinder energy.

seams_checked.note: Checked the declared page prerequisite and the actual supplier uses in pthm-qftx-n2-linear-monopole-bps-vortex-bound, Facts F3–F5 and Proof 3.1–4.1, against the three mathematical theorem statements. The consumer specializes e=g and ξ=2v², preserves arbitrary divisors, signed flux and gauge qualifications, and uses the mathematical cylinder collars directly only for embedded ends with a=p=0. General full-model ends invoke a separate full-model collar supplier. The mathematical suppliers have no reverse physical prerequisite; the consumer retains the linear-truncation scope and excludes nonlinear BPS saturation and quantum area-law conclusions.
